critical.finding: Two stories in one base scenario: the DCF and the yearly price path assume different returns on capital. The DCF charges growth capex of $528M in FY2027 and $553M in FY2028 (sales-to-capital 1.19 from history, i.e. an incremental after-tax ROIC of roughly 0.34 x 0.78 x 1.19 = about 30-40%), while company_path.base prices the same EPS at roic 0.95 ('almost no capital needed', capex ~$7M a year). The result: base year-1 price 288 (43.1x FY2028 EPS) against the DCF's own base value of 230 at 2027-12-31, and a 5-year base +311% resting on the path, not on the DCF. Either the DCF's reinvestment is wrong (the business really needs ~no capex, only receivables) or the path's 95% is wrong; both cannot hold in the same scenario.
critical.where: companies/RDDT/out/casefile.json val.case.scenarios[base].periods[*].growth_capex and assumption 'reinvestment' vs company_path.scenarios.base.roic=0.95 (position/path.json base)

Re-run ticker-value and re-render the table; until then the base yearly row is a draft.

critical.finding: The bear row shows a gain that the bear's own DCF contradicts. The table's 5-year potential row says bear +35% (path: 101 in year 1 rising to 124, at 21-22x forward EPS from roic 0.30), while the DCF bear values the share at 64.6 today and 74.4 at 2029-12-31, i.e. a loss of about 20-30%. The owner's buy test depends on 'a bear case he can live with', so a bear row of +35% would mislead him. In addition a 21x forward multiple in a bear of a shrinking audience is above where the stock trades today (13x FY2027 consensus EPS, 18.8x trailing on 2%-tax EPS) and near the own-history low of 18.7 set before the traffic shock; the bear is therefore more optimistic than the price.

open_critical.finding: Vested in-the-money options are still not in the share count: the position inputs have no option instrument (FORECAST_OPTIONS has no capital_events/options key and no DEBT_LIKE_KINDS kind fits, so it cannot be done without relabeling). 10-Q note 11: 5,604,522 vested options at a weighted strike of 39.29 (9,611,808 outstanding at 41.73). Treasury method: about 3.2M net shares at the 92.2 quote (1.7% of 193.1M) and about 4.6M (2.4%) at the base value of about 261, so the per-share values are about 2% too high. Unvested options and the 3.56M unvested RSUs/PRSUs are charged through sbc_pct, so adding them as shares would double count. Recorded as a gap in position/core.json.

Fair value went UP from 211 to 261 because the fix took the evidenced asset-light capital need (the DCF's old 1.19 sales-to-capital charged ~530M a year of growth capex that the filings do not show). The bear-only terminal growth of 2.5% sets aside the engine's convention (terminal growth = risk-free) for that one scenario, on evidence of a shrinking audience; a reviewer should accept or reject it.
Bear roic 0.30 is a stress assumption (about three times the evidenced capital per dollar of sales), labelled unproven.
